items.situation: Open the conversation. First sentence only.
tips: I want to be candid with you about the monthly report.
Candid, not honest. Honest suggests the alternative was lying.

items.situation: Name the behaviour with evidence, not with an adjective.
tips: It has been late seven months out of eight.
A number a stranger could check.

items.situation: Show the cost, using a conditional.
tips: If it arrived on the Friday, corporate would have the numbers before the call.
Past form for something that has not happened.

items.situation: He says nobody told him the deadline. Take your share in one sentence.
tips: Then that is on me. Nobody set expectations properly.
Taking the share does not lower the standard.

items.situation: He pushes back on sending an incomplete report. Hold the line.
tips: A report with two gaps on Friday is worth more to me than a perfect one on Tuesday.
Give the reason, not the order.
I am going to document what we agreed today.
The agreement is not the end. The record is.

listenings.text: I want to correct something almost everybody in this room believes. An improvement plan is not the paperwork you do before you let somebody go. If that is what it is in your organisation, then you are using it as a legal shield and your people know it. A real one has three things in it. A behaviour, described so precisely that a stranger could tell you whether it happened. A date, which is usually thirty, sixty or ninety days. And the support the company is putting in, which is the part people leave blank. If the company puts nothing in, you are not asking for a turnaround, you are asking for a miracle. And one more thing. If this is the first the person is hearing about it, the plan is not the problem. The eleven months of silence before it are the problem.

The feedback that changed how I work was four sentences long and my director gave it standing up, on a Tuesday, in a corridor. She said, you answer every question with a longer question. People leave your meetings without a decision and they think it is their fault. If you gave one answer before you asked anything back, half of your meetings would be shorter. And then she said, that is it, go. What made it land was not the corridor and it was not the four sentences. It was that she described something I do, not something I am. She did not say I was indecisive. She said I answer questions with questions, and I could check that. I went back through my last five meetings and she was right every time.
